players.note: A little worried about how this offense will look without Caleb. If he's out for a month and Swift is putting up duds in your lineup, that's going to be tough to weather.
I question this offense's true ceiling, but Nico will be back (possibly as soon as Week 4), and he'll be so far and away the WR1 that it's not even funny.
This offense is a disaster, and Hampton isn't the workhorse we thought he'd be. He's not getting many high-value touches, either.
With the injury, I'd rather get ahead of things and sell now.
Hasn't had a blowup game yet, but he's been completely fine and looks like the top guy in this backfield. The Jags will have a monster game or two very soon.
We'll see what the injury report says this week, but this Jets offense has some life, and Wilson is Geno's guy. If Wilson is only out a week or two, I'm holding onto him.
When your HC tells his wife to take you in fantasy, you know you're set to smash. Things will trend up from here.
Top pass-catcher and Brissett's safety net; higher PPR ceiling than most low-end WR1s.
Single biggest positional advantage of any player in fantasy
This guy has lost all his juice; there's nothing left in the tank. He's posting egregious efficiency numbers, and Woody Marks has looked more explosive thus far.
He's going to shoulder a heavy load with Jonathon Brooks injured, but he's mostly an uninspiring rusher. I don't think he possesses that difference-making ceiling.
This offense is going to score a ton of points this year, and most of it will be through the air. Not a complete zero on the ground, either.
Looks slow, stiff, and ultimately a shell of himself. He had a nice Week 3, but it was against a weak Dolphins defense. I'm not confident that volume continues.
What's up with this LAC offense? It's hard to watch, but I am still
The Browns look relatively competent, and Judkins is one of the few true NFL workhorses. The touchdowns should come eventually.
Kalif Raymond remains a focal point, but Luther Burden should separate himself from the pack over time.
He's going to miss far too much time. Unless you're 3-0 and rolling, sell AJB and get some win-now production.

Wicks and Doubs are gone, Reed is hurt, Jacobs is out indefinitely, and this offensive line is atrocious. Love will have to air it out to hang in these games, and he's looking Golden's way frequently.
Stuck in a committee, and I don't see him getting out of that committee anytime soon.
Josh Downs can be a PPR scam, and he's running nearly every route for the first time in his career. Wheels up.
17 targets in a game aren't sustainable, but Wilson has proven he's a clear top-two option in this offense (behind Trey McBride). You can start him with confidence.
A top-two option in a Josh Allen-led offense that can explode in any given week.
Out for an extended period with a hamstring injury, and wasn't even good enough to keep Kamara off the field.
Two-down plodder who doesn't really get many high-value touches. The JCM experience is a frustrating one week over week, and I'm ready to move on.
This guy is a complete non-factor now. Jaylen Waddle is the clear WR1 in this offense, and Bo Nix barely has the tools to feed him alone
Kellen Moore's air-raid offense is very fantasy-friendly, and Shough has wheels on top of this. The perfect combo.
Were we a bit premature in crowning Drake Maye the next great quarterback? He has looked beyond awful so far. I'm losing faith quickly.
Brutal start, yet again...but I'm confident he'll have a 20+ point game at some point. Wait to sell following the spike week; the return you can get right now is minimal.

Maybe the biggest disappointment to start the season. But don't get it twisted; Loveland is uber-talented, and he's an every-down player. The fantasy production will come, even if it's not to the level we once expected.
The old man can still play! Rice is finally back to his old self, but Kelce is still the second option.
He's purely a bench stash for now, but Makai Lemon has the ceiling to be a PPR monster and the top pass catcher in this offense. Yes, above DeVonta Smith. Don't give up on him yet!
Finger injury in Week 3, but had a big Week 2 performance. We'll see if he can build on that; feels very much boom or bust to me.
Sacrificial X. He's not startable in any situation so long as he's on the Cardinals. Sell for any return. (It's better than dropping!)
